cards.question: What is the New Packaging Sourcing proposal, and what kind of evidence is it?
cards.criterion: Attribute to the proposal (a Markdown file for review in /Ontology UseCases, pinned by item id and SHA-256, captured 16 Oct 2026): a Ross-attributed walkthrough of how a new packaging item should be sourced, with eleven target stages confirmed on 16 Oct 2026 and six proposed business rules P1 to P6 put to Vince (proposed, pending Vince). Say that approval of the rules is not evidenced, that its introduction counts five rules while its table lists six, that its six build tasks are proposals, and that its Portal and BC references come from a system map last checked on 30 Sep 2026 and need code verification, so every Portal or BC statement in it is unverified. Call it a stakeholder proposal, not a decision, an implementation instruction or authority to act.

cards.question: Which business rules does the proposal put to Vince, and what is their status?
cards.criterion: Name the six as the proposal's (proposed_rules): P1 three sign-offs before a packaging quote is approved; P2 part creation at approval with the order prerequisites; P3 linking the part to its project; P4 allocating cost to the component that carries it; P5 who requests and records a vendor deposit; P6 a PO before the vendor PI and the PI matched before payment. Each is proposed, pending Vince: an answer never describes any of them as decided, as current practice or as built, and notes the five-versus-six count mismatch in the proposal.

cards.question: What quote evidence does the proposal require from a packaging vendor?
cards.criterion: Per the proposal: currency, MOQ, lead time, INCO term with its named place, country of origin, the vendor's item number and the case-pack, with the drawing and sample evidence behind the quote, for each component. Per the Sept 30 map (unverified): a supplier item holds cost, price tiers, MOQ, lead time, INCO terms, origin and one delivery cost; a named place and a case-pack are not named there. An answer keeps the proposal's requirement apart from what the Portal holds and gives no figures.

cards.question: Which sign-offs does the proposal require before a packaging quote is approved, and where are they recorded?
cards.criterion: The proposal requires customer, QC and costing sign-offs (P1, proposed, pending Vince). It does not evidence an approval, and where each sign-off is recorded today is unknown (PS-GAP-01). An answer names the three roles, not people, and reports the record as unknown rather than inferring it from a sample status.

cards.question: When does the proposal have the packaging part created, and what can the Portal do today?
cards.criterion: The proposal: the part is created at approval from the approved quote and linked to its project (P2 and P3, proposed, pending Vince). The Sept 30 map (unverified): linking a sourcing request needs an accepted sample, a drawing and an existing packaging item; the Portal has no way to create a new packaging item and no P-#### number series. An answer keeps the target, the map's claim and the unchecked code apart.

cards.question: What must exist before a packaging part may be ordered, and does the purchase order carry the HS code?
cards.criterion: The proposal: a drawing and an HS code before the part is ordered (P2, proposed, pending Vince). The Sept 30 map (unverified): the HS code is set on the product when the request is linked, purchase order lines carry no HS code and none is sent to BC. An answer says whether a given part has an HS code only from public.app_product and never claims the PO line or BC carries it.

cards.question: How should prices be recorded when the components of one packaging item ship separately?
cards.criterion: The proposal: a price per component when the parts ship separately, and the cost allocated to the component that carries it (P4, proposed, pending Vince). The Sept 30 map (unverified): a supplier item carries one cost with price tiers per supplier and product. An answer describes the price structure (per component, currency, unit, tier) and states no price figures.

cards.question: What must exist before a vendor proforma invoice, and what is checked on it before payment?
cards.criterion: The proposal: a PO is issued before the vendor's PI, and the PI's price, quantity and terms are checked against the PO before anything is paid (P6, proposed, pending Vince). The Sept 30 map (unverified): the PO has no PI number field; BC purchaseInvoices are posted invoices, not proforma invoices. Where a PI is kept and who checks it is unknown (PS-GAP-06, PS-GAP-07). An answer never treats a posted BC invoice as the PI.

cards.question: How does the proposal want vendor deposits handled, and what exists for them today?
cards.criterion: The proposal: purchasing requests the deposit, with the account manager stating urgency, and it is recorded in BC as a prepayment on the purchase order (P5, proposed, pending Vince). The Sept 30 map (unverified): vendor prepayment is not built; BC Prepayment % on the PO is never set; AP handles deposits in BC by hand; OrderPrepayment is customer (AR) only. The Workbench's purchaseOrders allowlist has no prepayment field and vendorPayments apply to invoices, so an answer reports a PO's deposit as unknown.

cards.question: How does an approved packaging part reach a purchase order in the proposal's workflow?
cards.criterion: Per the proposal: brief, component BOM, vendor RFQs, quote, drawing and sample evidence, approval, handoff to purchasing, part creation, assembly demand, requisition and PO, then the deposit. Per the Sept 30 map (unverified): only the requisition is approved, a PO has no approval of its own and sending it records no send time. An answer traces a part from public.app_product to public.app_purchase_requisition and public.app_purchase_order and reports a step it cannot see as a gap, never a match.

cards.question: What does the proposal leave open, and what must a cutover handle?
cards.criterion: Open per the proposal: whether a label states 100mL or 3.5 fl.oz; which entity purchases and which pays; whether the DDP multiplier counts freight and duty twice; how far the sourcing-request workflow has been used historically. Cutover: packaging item identifiers, open assembly orders and POs, and vendor deposits. An answer lists these as open and does not answer them from the proposal.

cards.question: Can a DDP vendor quote be double counted by the landed-cost formula?
cards.criterion: The proposal raises it as an open question. The Sept 30 map (unverified): the quote-time landed cost is (tier price + duty) times a multiplier plus freight, with freight added per unit, so a DDP price that already includes freight and duty could be counted twice. An answer reports the risk as unconfirmed, computes no landed cost and names the question for Vince (PS-GAP-09).

cards.question: How was the P-02486 bottle and cap cost allocated, and what does the proposal correct?
cards.criterion: The proposal says the cost of the bottle and its cap was assigned to the bottle alone, and proposes allocating it to each component (P4, proposed, pending Vince). The P-02486 item records are not supplied (MO-02), so the allocation is the proposal's claim, unverified. An answer quotes no price and does not reconstruct the allocation from other records.

cards.question: What mismatches does the proposal report on PI-SWC025623?
cards.criterion: The proposal cites mismatches between PI-SWC025623 and what was ordered; the PI is not supplied (MO-03), so the mismatches and the PO they belong to are unverified. An answer attributes them to the proposal, lists no amounts and treats a PI-to-PO join as unseen.

cards.question: Which vendor deposit does the proposal cite, and was it recorded as a prepayment on the purchase order?
cards.criterion: The proposal cites a vendor deposit; the deposit record is not supplied (MO-04), and the Sept 30 map says deposits are booked in BC by hand without a PO prepayment (unverified). An answer reports whether it was recorded as a prepayment as unknown and states no amount.
